findings.reason: naming the guard and `resolve_project_repository` reduces §2 from a vague re-design to a one-line change at a named site and corrects the plan's stated defect mechanism.
findings.text: §2's causal model is wrong: it says the read-only resolutions "are simply not reached when `dry_run` is set", but `plan_dispatch` has no `dry_run` parameter and the dry-run branch of the CLI (`reckon/cli.py:2059`) calls this same function; the resolutions are skipped only by the guard `if repo is not None and project_mount_repository(project) is not None:` at dispatch.py:5253–5255, because the CLI hands `--repo` through unresolved while the real `dispatch()` resolves the mount first at dispatch.py:6617 — so the dry run already resolves the plan, section and review whenever `--repo` is given, and the fix is to resolve the mount in `plan_dispatch` as `dispatch()` does (via `resolve_project_repository`, dispatch.py:249), not to "move the dry run's stopping line"

findings.reason: the section must name the two owners to reconcile and fix the trigger conditions there, rather than add a new resolution path.
findings.text: member roster resolution already exists twice: `plan_dispatch` resolves the roster and raises D14 only inside `if member and (local or backend_override is not None or default_backend_override is not None)` (dispatch.py:5318–5355) while `dispatch()` resolves it for any named member (dispatch.py:7058–7071) — §3's "one answer, not two" is a consolidation of these two owners onto the shared lookup `ledger.member` (reckon/ledger.py:1475), and the plan names neither; the recorded decision ("project alone" vs "repository required") is answerable from the roster shape, since `ledger.member` keys a member by (project, id) and carries no repository dimension

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the change is a modification of the one shared resolver `plan_dispatch` (reckon/crew/dispatch.py:5198), whose interface already hides routing, the authority join, the plan/review gates and admission behind `DispatchPlan`; no new module or wrapper is proposed.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §3 asks to make member resolution single-valued but names neither of the two existing owners of that resolution (reckon/crew/dispatch.py:5318 in `plan_dispatch` and reckon/crew/dispatch.py:7058 in `dispatch`), so the fix risks becoming a third site.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 1470, cli_options 317, mcp_views 33, refusal_families 23; no section adds a CLI option, MCP view, public definition or refusal family — §2/§3 reuse the existing `plan-unavailable`/`plan-review-missing`/D14 codes and their already-shared payloads (reckon/cli.py:2106 / 2305), and §4 adds only documentation.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — the plan claims the resolution calls "already exist on the real path and are simply not reached when dry_run is set", but the shared resolver is already invoked by the dry-run branch and the skip is a `repo is not None` guard, not a dry_run flag; the mechanism (`resolve_project_repository`, `plan_dispatch`) is never named.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — the plan extends `plan_dispatch`/the dispatch CLI rather than layering a parallel preview resolver over them, so there is no wrapper whose justification is missing.
